user.title: Dayline
user.description: Pick the calendars that belong on the wall. Calendars you leave out are never fetched — that is the point. You can add weather and a to-do list now or later.

menu_options.sources: Sources — which calendars, weather, to-do list
menu_options.sentences: Sentences — what the house does, in plain words

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Removing a calendar also forgets its label and priority.

calendars.title: Calendars
calendars.description:
The label is what the pill on the card says; calendars sharing a label share a pill. Order matters: when two calendars carry the same event worded differently, the first one listed supplies the wording.

Set the role to “schedule” for a calendar that drives automations rather than describing people's plans — its events become House rows and each event's description becomes the sage sentence.

sentences.title: Sentences
sentences.description: What the house will do, in plain words, matched against any text in an event's title. First match wins, so order is precedence.

sentence_edit.title: Sentence
sentence_edit.description: Say the consequence, not the scene name: “Entry unlocks on her arrival”, not “scene.arrival_1”.

data.sticky: Stays until someone acts on it

recent.title: What just happened
recent.description: Short-lived lines explaining changes the house made on its own. Only listed entities can ever produce one, and only when something other than a person caused the change.

recent_edit.title: Explanation
recent_edit.description: One sentence per entity per state. Plain words, no entity ids.

tuning.title: Tuning
tuning.description:
Similarity is how much of two titles must match before they are treated as one event — 0.8 is strict. Lower it if duplicates slip through, raise it if unrelated events start merging.

Leave the templates empty for sensible defaults.
